Yes.  A framework of breaking up the entire economy into large cohorts that are mostly homogenous in terms of their response to change and then adding them up bottoms up while also going top down as been table stakes for macro for decades.  It was happening in 2010 when I first became aware of that method. 

What i find troubling is the weighting I see amongst many is the overweighting of the rich saver cohort. It has absolutely 100% grown in influence a lot.  But is still tiny relative to actually tight monetary policy that persists for a few months 

 If you do what i do and what is table stakes for macro we can still have quite different cohort level views and the weightings and bottoms up process can be vastly different.

I guess the question is.  If your goal was to durably bring inflation back to target and you were able to use all of the Fed tools with no restraint or oversight how would you accomplish your goal.  

Here's what I would do.
I would sell 50bn of Treasuries and 50BN of MBS monthly and use the proceeds to purchase bills.  If the Treasury cut 10's -30's issuance or increased buybacks I would increase my selling bond for bond. My goal would be to crush the asset market and increase the cost of corporate funding.

I would maintain short rates at about current levels because they are less effective to achieve my goal.
